notes: Same method as 20260902/20260903/20260904: the data lives in the Next.js App Router RSC flight payload embedded in the leaderboard document, not in a separate XHR/fetch endpoint. window.__next_f is emptied after hydration, so the 56 <script> tags containing `self.__next_f.push(...)` were read out of the DOM and evaluated with a stubbed push() to capture the (id, stringChunk) pairs. Concatenated flight text was 3,572,060 chars.

The flight text again contains TWO top-level "models":[ arrays. The slim model-picker list is at offset 10,592; the full leaderboard payload is at offset 298,239. This scrape took the LAST occurrence and asserted, inside the page before saving, that the first element carries both `intelligenceIndex` and `gpqa` keys and that the array has more than 100 entries. Extraction used balanced-bracket text slicing (string-aware, not regex) and JSON.parse in-browser, saved straight to disk via evaluate_script filePath.
raw.json is the verbatim `models` array from that payload: 643 entries, 3,255,665 bytes, 96 keys per model.

The missing-value sentinel reverted: today's payload uses the literal string "$undefined" again (the 20260904 payload used JSON null). Both forms, plus real null, are treated as absent when building normalized.json, so behaviour is unchanged either way.

DEEPER THAN 20260904 - new benchmark rows: AA-Openness Index (opennessBreakdown.opennessIndex, 314 models) and AA-Multilingual Index (multilingualBreakdown.average, 112 models). These two are single summary scalars lifted out of otherwise-nested breakdown objects; their per-category sub-scores stay nested and unexploited.

DEEPER THAN 20260904 - new metric rows: training_tokens_trillions (trainingTokensTrillions, 150 models; the field carried the same 150 values on 20260904 but was never captured), intelligence_index_reasoning_tokens_per_task and intelligence_index_answer_tokens_per_task (55 models each, lifted from intelligenceIndexOutputTokensPerTask).

FIXED vs 20260904: intelligenceIndexCostPerTask and intelligenceIndexOutputTokensPerTask are nested objects, not scalars, and the 20260904 normalized.json stored the whole object in the `score` field. This scrape stores real numbers instead: intelligence_index_cost_per_task_usd now comes from intelligenceIndexCostPerTask.cost.total and intelligence_index_output_tokens_per_task from intelligenceIndexOutputTokensPerTask.output. The per-evaluation arrays inside those objects remain unexploited.

DEEPER THAN 20260904 - new per-record attribute fields, all read from the payload and omitted when absent: model_slug, provider_country, is_reasoning, is_open_weights, deprecated, size_class, param_class, price_class. Nothing from the old record shape was removed.

NOT flattened into normalized.json (left as unexploited depth, stated rather than invented): gdpvalBreakdown (Elo, avgTurns, 95% CI, lastUpdated), omniscienceBreakdown (per-domain accuracy / omniscience / hallucination rate), evalTokenCounts and intelligenceIndexTokenCounts (per-eval and aggregate token counts), the per-language entries of multilingualBreakdown, the component scores of opennessBreakdown, and the `evaluations` arrays inside intelligenceIndexCostPerTask / intelligenceIndexOutputTokensPerTask. These are nested objects, not single scalars, and do not fit the flat (model, benchmark/metric, score) row schema without a schema change.

Other payload fields deliberately not turned into rows because they are identifiers or presentation data, not measurements: id, shortName, modelCreatorId/Slug/Color/Logo, licenseName, licenseUrl, huggingfaceUrl, openrouterApiId, and the eight input/output modality booleans.
`rank` is present only on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index records and is derived here by sorting all 630 models that report a non-null index descending; it is not a rank published by the site.
`cost_usd` on every record is the model-level blended price per 1M tokens at a 3:1 input:output ratio (field price1mBlended0To3To1), attached as cost context; it is not a per-benchmark cost.
`date` is the model release date (releaseDate) reported by the site, not the scrape date.
Score scales are as published: eval scores are fractions 0-1 (e.g. gpqa), index values are on their own scales. No rescaling applied.
Null and "$undefined" values were omitted rather than filled.

Small upward moves in populated counts: latency and output-speed metrics 333 -> 337 models, output_speed_median_answer_tokens_per_second 331 -> 335, MLCR 80 -> 83, cache_hit_price / cache_hit_discount 247 -> 248. Small downward move: the seven price metrics 440 -> 439.

Browser session note for future runs: this MCP session had roughly ten agents scraping concurrently and the shared 'selected page' pointer was stolen on almost every call. About 120 consecutive select_page + evaluate_script attempts landed on another agent's page before one hit this page's URL. Pure session contention, not a site-side problem. The whole scrape was therefore packed into a single evaluate_script that extracts, validates and saves raw.json in one shot, so only one pointer win was needed; all normalisation was done locally afterwards without touching the browser.
